methodologyNotes: Roster covers twelve air (fan) bikes spanning budget home models to commercial/CrossFit-gym machines, verified 2026-08-09 directly against manufacturer/brand product pages (Assault Fitness, Rogue Fitness, Schwinn, Titan Fitness, Xebex, REP Fitness, Bells of Steel, Marcy, Sole Fitness, Life Fitness/Hammer Strength, Concept2, Torque Fitness), corroborated where noted by authorized resellers (IronCompany, GetRXd). Three seed products from the suggested list did not correspond to real, currently-sold items and were replaced with the closest real equivalent from the same brand (documented per-product in provenance): "Xebex AB-3" does not exist as a model code — replaced with Xebex's actual entry-level commercial air bike, the Air Bike 1000 (AB-1000-E); "REP Fitness Aero Bike" does not exist — REP's current air bike is the Strive Air Bike featuring VPR; "Marcy Air-1" does not exist — Marcy's current fan/air bike is the NS-1000. Two further substitutions were adversarial corrections to seeds that are real products but wrong for this category or brand: "Sole SB900" is a magnetic-resistance indoor cycle, not an air/fan bike, so it was replaced with Sole's actual air-resistance model, the SB750 Air Bike (a Costco Canada exclusive, hence priceUsd is null); "Life Fitness Assault" does not exist — Life Fitness has no product line called Assault (that is an unrelated company, Assault Fitness), so the entry was replaced with Life Fitness's own commercial air bike, sold under its Hammer Strength sub-brand, the HD Air Bike; "ProForm Carbon CB Air Bike" does not exist — ProForm's current Carbon line is magnetic-resistance only and ProForm's older air-resistance model (WhirlWind) has been discontinued for years with no listed successor, so the entry was replaced with a real, currently-sold commercial air bike from a comparable brand, the Torque Fitness Stealth Air Bike. fanSizeIn and driveType are left null wherever no manufacturer page explicitly states a fan-blade diameter or drive mechanism, rather than inferring from similar models. Prices are the clearest current price shown on the brand's own site (sale price where a site displays one, with the regular/list price recorded in priceNote); accessedAt 2026-08-09 throughout.

products.name: REP Strive Air Bike featuring VPR
products.priceNote: MSRP (US) per repfitness.com official product page.
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: REP Fitness does not sell a product called "Aero Bike." REP's actual, newly launched air bike (available June 30, 2026) is the Strive Air Bike featuring VPR (Variable Pitch Resistance), which mechanically adjusts fan-blade angle across 8 resistance levels rather than depending purely on cadence. REP's own page confirms 350 lb capacity, 146 lb unit weight, dual-stage belt drive, 14-gauge steel frame, ANT+ heart-rate compatibility, and the stated dimensions. No fan-blade diameter is published (VPR fan design differs from a fixed-diameter fan), so fanSizeIn is left null.
